summary.headline: Veranda Q1 FY27 revenue rose 42% YoY to INR150 crore and PAT to INR34 crore, with commerce demerger listing guided for September 2026.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 42% YoY to about INR150 crore and enrollments rose 35% to about 1.03 lakh students. EBITDA was about INR54 crore with a margin near 36% as stated, but management acknowledged the reported EBITDA growth of 10% was flattered by a INR17 crore one-time other income in Q1 FY26; excluding it, EBITDA grew about 30%. PAT rose to INR34 crore from INR5.9 crore, helped by a INR7.35 crore tax reversal tied to an intra-group merger. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR670 crore revenue, INR260 crore EBITDA and INR144 crore PAT, and said the Commerce demerger NCLT order is expected shortly with listing before end-September 2026.

segments.name: Commerce Test Prep
segments.commentary: Revenue INR108.6 crore (+53% YoY), EBITDA INR42.7 crore (~40% margin). Offline revenue about INR330 crore and online about INR120 crore annualised, offline margin ~35% and online ~45-48%. Managed commerce colleges at about 17 now, to add 15 more this year.

segments.name: Government test prep
segments.commentary: Revenue INR32.5 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA nearly INR4 crore vs near breakeven last quarter. Target of INR95-100 crore EBITDA over four to five years; Karnataka expansion planned in FY27.

segments.name: Academic / K-12
segments.commentary: Revenue INR12.2 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR9.2 crore (+53% YoY). Manages six schools with over 5,400 students; preschool managed operations to be entered in FY27.

segments.name: SNVA Veranda (associate stake)
segments.commentary: Vocational/higher-ed businesses (Edureka, Six Phrase) were moved into SNVA Veranda; management expects value unlock, with the stake to sit in the non-commerce entity post demerger. No figures given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: revenue about INR670 crore (FY26: INR482 crore), EBITDA about INR260 crore (FY26: INR204 crore), PAT about INR144 crore (FY26: INR130 crore).
Commerce FY27: revenue about INR450 crore, EBITDA about INR215 crore, PAT about INR110 crore.
Non-commerce FY27: revenue about INR220 crore, EBITDA INR46 crore, PAT INR34 crore.
Management cited EBITDA margin of about 38.8% for FY27 (per analyst reading of guidance); expects margins to recover in Q2 and Q3 as college and marketing spends mature.

Commerce demerger: NCLT order expected imminently after July 20 hearing (orders reserved); next NCLT hearing 17 August 2026; listing targeted by end-September 2026. Shareholders receive 1 JK Shah Commerce Education share per Veranda share.
Commerce long-term aspiration: revenue above INR1,000 crore by FY30.
capex_capacity: Offline commerce network at over 105 centres; 50 new commerce colleges under management in pipeline; plan to add 15 managed commerce colleges in FY27 (doubling from about 17).
Commerce Virtuals (live and recorded digital format for Class 11-12) recently launched for pan-India reach without physical infrastructure.
Government test prep: Group 1 offline programmes, junior IAS, subscription magazines; expansion into Karnataka in FY27.
Planned offline presence in UP, Bihar, Rajasthan and Gujarat to reduce regional concentration.
Managed schools: six schools, 5,400+ students; preschool managed operations to start in FY27.
demand_pricing: Enrollments +35% YoY vs collections +27%; management attributed gap to subject-wise commerce classes, which raise enrollment counts with lower per-enrollment billing.
Q1 collections INR165 crore vs revenue INR150 crore; about INR15 crore of advances deferred under Ind AS 11 to later quarters.
Managed school revenue jump attributed to ~10% student growth plus start-of-year book and service sales (~20% uplift in Q1).
Guided ARPU increase of 7-8% a year and 10% student growth in FY27 as EBITDA drivers, plus 15 new colleges.
Commerce positioned as number one across CA, CS, CMA, ACCA; management claims undisputed leadership in pedigree, alumni, centres and ranks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable quarterly finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Mohasin Khan guided INR7.5-8 crore per quarter after refinancing; EBITDA excludes finance cost, so no finance savings sit in the EBITDA bridge.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tax swing to a credit of about INR3 crore from about INR8 crore a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Following an intra-group merger of a subsidiary into the parent, management reversed INR7.35 crore of tax related to earlier years; described as current tax, not a DTA write-off.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline QoQ and how will FY27 38.8% margin be reached?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited doubled college expansion spend, pre-demerger advertising for the commerce brand, and initial work on 15 new colleges, all expensed in Q1; expects benefit in next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and timing of the NCLT approval and listing?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders were reserved at the 20 July hearing; affidavit filed on the appointed date query; next hearing 17 August. Management expects order within about a week, then ROC filing in 3-4 days, a record date one week later, and listing before end-September.

qa_highlights.question: Will non-commerce be valued lower because it carries all the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects the commerce entity to command the highest sector multiple as the leader; government test prep should earn a good multiple, K-12 less so. No numbers provided on valuation.

qa_highlights.question: What is the offline/online split and margins in commerce?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline about INR330 crore and online about INR120 crore (roughly 3:1 offline to online per management); offline margin ~35%, online ~45-48%.
